paper_metadata.title: Investigation of mechanical properties and high temperature wear resistance of CoFeNi1.5VZr0.4Six high entropy alloys optimized by Si alloying

evidence.quote: The current work studies the mechanical properties and high-temperature wear resistance of CoFeNi1.5VZr0.4Six high entropy alloys by Si alloying.
The worn surface morphologies of CoFeNi1.5VZr0.4Six HEAs: (a) Si00 HEA, (b) Si02 HEA, (c) Si04 HEA and (d) Si06HEA at 400 ℃ .
Ingots of CoFeNi1.5VZr0.4Six (x = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, denoted as Si00, Si02, Si04 and Si06, respectively. atomic %) HEAs were fabricated by arc melting

HEAs were fabricated by arc melting a mixture of pure elements (purity > 99.9 wt%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere. All HEAs ingots were flipped over and remelted at least six times to ensure composition homogeneity.
The XRD pattern of the Si00 HEA shows diffraction peaks of FCC phase and Ni7Zr2 phase.
the light gray region corresponds to the FCC phase, and the dark gray region corresponds to the Ni7Zr2 phase
The XRD pattern of the Si00 HEA shows diffraction peaks of FCC phase and Ni7Zr2 phase.
The peak intensity of the Ni7Zr2 phase decreases slightly in the XRD pattern of Si02 HEA (Fig. 1b), indicative of a reduced Ni7Zr2 phase content in the Si02 HEA.
Consequently, Si04 and Si06 HEAs consist of a combination of FCC and silicide phases.
the silicide phase consists of Si, Zr and Ni
Consequently, Si04 and Si06 HEAs consist of a combination of FCC and silicide phases.
In the case of the Si06 HEA, irrespective of whether inside or outside the wear mark, the primary component observed was SiO2.

On the worn surface of Si00 HEA, Fe3O4 emerges as the primary constituent, and during the process of high-temperature friction, the less compact Fe3O4 tribo-layer experiences detachment from the surface, resulting in the generation of oxide debris and poor wear resistance.
Si00 and Si02 HEAs had similar typical lamellar eutectic structures.
the microstructure of the HEAs transformed from single eutectic structures to lamellar eutectic structures and herringbone structures with Si content increasing, as shown in the Si04 HEA
the microstructure converts to complete dendritic structure in Si06 HEA.

evidence.quote: No discernible signs of plastic deformation can be observed on the cross-section of the worn surface of Si06 HEA. Below the worn surface, transverse bands of refined grains are evident, indicating the occurrence of recrystallization.
Adding a small amount of Si (x ≤ 0.2) reduces the microhardness of the HEAs from 499.3 HV to 455.8 HV at room temperature.
Adding a small amount of Si (x ≤ 0.2) reduces the microhardness of the HEAs from 499.3 HV to 455.8 HV at room temperature.
upon further increasing the Si content, the microhardness rises significantly, reaching 624.7HV for the Si06 HEA.
the Si06 HEA displays a substantial decrease in the coefficient of friction, dropping from 0.64 at room temperature to 0.37 at 800°C.

the Si06 HEA demonstrates a significantly lower wear rate of 1.27 × 10^-5 mm3·N^-1·m^-1, representing a nearly seven-fold improvement in wear resistance compared to the other three HEAs.
at 800°C, the wear rate of the Si06 HEA measures 1.21 × 10^-6 mm3·N^-1·m^-1, which is 22 times lower compared to the Si00 HEA lacking Si (2.67 × 10^-5 mm3·N^-1·m^-1).

Si alloying increased the hardness of HEA due to solid solution strengthening and phase transformation.
At room temperature, the main wear mechanism of HEAs is abrasive wear.
The worn surface of Si04 HEA exhibits a combination of debris, plowing grooves, and a dark tribo-layer, indicating a combination of abrasive wear and oxidation wear as the main mechanisms.
